page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Main text in one column, with one marginal note in the right margin beside the first line of the Naphtali verse. The left edge shows part of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: te oled erunt in portione ejus. Ac notat Mosen in istum modum ei benedixisse, Et pedem suum oleo tinget. Deut.33.24.

Naphthali (est) cerva emissa, Ver.21. &c.] Per cervam emissam R.Salom.Intelligit vallem Genosar, seu Genesaret, quae fructus suos cito maturos reddit, sicut cerva, quae cursu velox est. LXX, pro cerva emissa vertunt ἔλαφος ἀπολελυμένη, i.e. virgultum resolutum, ut Hieronymus interpretatur, qui ait in Hebraeo esse, Nephthalim ager irriguus: ac significari, quod aquae calidae in ista nascantur tribu; sive quod super lacum Genesareth, et fluenta Jordanis irrigua sint. Hebraeos autem refert velle propter Tiberiadem, quae Legis videbatur habere noticiam, agrum irriguum, & eluquia pulchritudinis prophetari. Addit denique verba Hebraea [illegible, ~12 letters] Seluba transferri posse, cervam emissam, propter temperaneas fruges velocitatem terrae tiberiadis ostendens. Sed melius (inquit) si ad doctrinam Salvatoris eundem referamus, quod ibi vel maxime docuerit, ut in Evangelio quoque scriptum est. Haec Hieron. cujus postrema interpretatio verborum Hebraicorum, nempe cervus emissus (prout etiam habet Vulgata editio, etiamsi malim in foemi-nino; quemadmodum est in Hebraeo, cerva emissa) est verissima; nec intelligo quomodo vel virgultum resolutum, vel ager irriguus verbis Hebraicis significetur. Quod ad posteriorem versus partem attinet, R.Salom. eam intelligendam ait, sicut interpretatus est Onkelos, cujus paraphrasis ita habet, Naphthali, in terra bona cadet sors ejus; & possessio ejus erit fructifera: gratias agent, & benedicent super eos, scil. fructus. Sic Fagius vertit; at [illegible, ~4 letters] verti potest, super ista, scil. terram bonam, & possessionem

page.notes: Hebrew words in the text are largely illegible at this scan resolution and are marked where not readable. The marginal note at "Ver.21." is clear. Another faint marginal fragment on the right, around the middle of the page, is too blurred to read and is not transcribed. The last line "sessionem" is a catchword-like continuation and is kept as the last full line. The footnote "Onkelos" at the foot of the page is faint and may be a printed catchword; it is kept as a foot note with doubt.
